# P35.22 — Truthful claim identity: volatile fields leave the digest (L3 CP-1)

**Ticket:** `docs/tickets/302_P35.22__truthful-claim-identity.md`
(manifest row **302**, Round 11 / P35, sub-round 11B — `R11-L3-CP1`, the
L3-confidence-program's CP-1). Invoked `live_verification=false` — committed
code only; **no production re-ingest, no `/status/` post, no live parity
report**. Legs L2/L3 are queued (OM-20 conditional — operator authority /
next scheduled runs). Closes **F-504** (S1); requirement stamps:
**SIG-INGEST-003**, **SIG-INGEST-004**, SIG-EPIS-009 (context — P35.25 owns
the binding rule), **CONF-03a**, S6 **A-20**, **ADR-059** (the digest
mechanism extended — the contract's ADR-159 citation is an anchor mismatch,
recorded in **ADR-211**).
**Base:** `r11/P35.20b-freshness-classes-and-map-table-suppression` ·
**Gate:** OM-20 conditional (live legs only — none run in this change) ·
**Production mutations:** none.

## The defect (F-504)

`claim.content_digest` is claim identity — the `claim_content_digest_key`
partial unique index makes it the dedup key, and a re-observation of the same
fact must re-bind to it (a `claim_evidence` sighting), never mint a second id.
The digest was a whole-record sha256 minus `claim_id`/`sys_period`/
`recorded_at`, so **volatile acquisition detail sat in identity**: row
position, page/capture URL, capture digest, fetch time, upstream record-version
counters — and `valid_from`. Any of them churning minted another claim for an
unchanged fact; each mint counted as an independent support class. F-504
measured ≈2.2 M unresolved `camera_operator` and ≈1.9 M `located_in`-family
claims. Two secondary defects: emitter-side and sink-side minting were two
copies of the rule that could silently diverge, and the correction/recovery
paths used the same `content_digest` both to pin a stored ROW's state and to
mint a NEW claim's identity — two jobs the new scheme must split.

## What ships

- **`evidence/src/evidence/claim_identity.py` — the one identity function.**
  `claim_digest(record, temporal_class=…)` → `digest_base` → sha256 over
  compact sorted-keys JSON. `NEVER_IDENTITY_KEYS` strips the volatile classes
  recursively (row position, page/capture URL, capture/binding identity, fetch
  time, upstream version counters, envelope fields) at every level **except
  inside `value_json`** — the asserted payload is opaque; a mapping that loses
  every member to the projection is identical to an absent key. Every stripped
  value stays recorded — on `claim_evidence`/`evidence_capture`; only its
  identity role ends.
- **The `obs`/`ref` split is registry-read.** `temporal_class()` derives the
  class from the predicate's `vocab_predicate` row: `is_windowed` OR
  `resolution_strategy ∈ {interval_union, interval_intersection}` marks `obs`
  (the SIG-RECON-011 windowed family — the window IS the claim; its temporal
  qualifier stays in identity). `latest_observation_wins`/`max_support` are
  **ref** by design — ADR-R9-RESIGHT's mechanism reads recency from the latest
  sighting's capture `retrieved_at`, not from a qualifier on the claim;
  keeping `observed_at` in identity for them re-creates F-504.
  `vocab_predicate.is_windowed` exists in DDL but is unseeded — the strategy
  field is today's operative signal; `is_windowed` is honoured for when the
  registry populates it.
- **`value_json` canonicalisation, stored.** `assertion_from_record` stores
  `canonical_json(value_json)` — sorted keys, compact separators, NFC strings,
  exact-range integral floats as ints, `Decimal`/datetime canonical text —
  the same normalisation the digest consumes, so stored payload and minted
  identity never diverge.
- **`claim.payload_version` (sqitch `claim_payload_version`).** Nullable, no
  default, append-only-registered; records which normalisation produced each
  row's digest (`sig.claim-payload/1`, sealed into the digest base). No index
  change — `claim_content_digest_key` remains the dedup key. Existing rows
  keep their ids and carry `NULL` (CP-1's no-mass-re-mint invariant; the
  migration never recomputes a stored digest). Old duplicates' supersession is
  P35.23's merge/alias pass.
- **`db.claim_sink` delegates.** `content_digest` → `claim_digest`; the sink
  resolves each predicate's class lazily from `vocab_predicate`
  (`predicate_temporal_class`, cached). `legacy_row_digest` keeps the
  pre-P35.22 whole-row serialisation byte-identical — it serves only the
  correction-apply **staleness pins** (`intake_apply.claim_state_digest`,
  seed-correction target location): a pin verifies a recorded row, never
  mints. New correction/repair claims mint under the identity digest +
  `payload_version` like every other claim; `ops.seed_correction` locates a
  target under EITHER scheme (real seed rows are old-scheme; post-change rows
  are new-scheme).
- **Emitter-side parity harness** — `connectors/claim_identity_ingest.py`:
  `predicate_temporal_classes()` (registry YAML → class map),
  `emitted_claim_digest`/`reconcile_rows`/`emitted_row_key`,
  `read_rows`/`write_rows` over the declared `ingest_claim_reconcile.csv`
  schema (`RECONCILE_FIELDS`), and `diff_minting` → `rebound`/`minted`/
  `divergent` per logical row key. `connectors.replay.diff_claim_sets` +
  `replay_fingerprint` and `evidence.ingest_run.canonical_claim_tuple`/
  `claim_set_fingerprint` run the same class-aware projection — replay diffs
  no longer flag volatile churn as claim changes.
- **The `/status/` API-basis notice is drafted, not posted.** S6 A-20's
  disclosure is leg L2 — it posts when the next scheduled runs actually mint
  under the new identity. The drafted sentence + sha256 sit in the run
  ledger (`docs/build/runs/P35.22.md`), verbatim-confirmable at the live
  sitting; the engineering change renders nothing public ahead of the
  behaviour it describes.
- **`ops/quality.py` GQ-02 seam text** updated to name what landed (the shared
  identity + the minting-diff harness) and what remains (the rotating-source
  capture-replay telemetry leg — queued live work).
- **ADR-211** records the decisions and the contract-artifact deviations:
  the ADR-159 anchor mismatch (the mechanism is ADR-059), the registry-read
  `obs`/`ref` derivation (no literal `obs`/`ref` column exists), the absent
  `docs/build/planning/…/data/ingest_claim_reconcile.csv` (schema declared by
  `RECONCILE_FIELDS`; fixture under `tests/connectors/fixtures/
  claim_identity/`), and the `value_json` storage-form normalisation.

## Tests (fails-if-removed)

- `tests/evidence/test_claim_identity_projection.py` — volatile classes at
  every level; `value_json` ordering/representation/NFC/Decimal/datetime
  canonicalisation; `null`≡absent; serialised-string `value_json` parity;
  `obs` keeps / `ref` drops the temporal qualifier; `payload_version` seals
  the base.
- `tests/db/test_claim_identity.py` (live PG) — a re-observation differing
  only in volatile fields inserts +0 and adds a `claim_evidence` sighting;
  a `valid_from`-only change re-binds; `obs`-class qualifiers are identity;
  new rows carry `payload_version`; stored digests are never rewritten.
- `tests/connectors/test_claim_identity_ingest.py` — emitter-vs-sink digest
  parity over the `ingest_claim_reconcile.csv` fixture (two re-binds + one
  genuine mint → `rebound 2, minted 1, divergent 0`); the CSV codec round-trip.
- `tests/connectors/test_data_driven.py` +
  `test_coarse_dataset_adapters.py` — the re-ingest tests now pin the
  truthful semantics: unchanged release rows re-bind, only changed values
  mint.
- `tests/partner_fixtures.py::golden_digest` — the partner goldens pin
  pre-P35.22 whole-row digests, so they verify under `legacy_row_digest`
  explicitly.

## Boundaries

No production ingest, no `/status/` post, no live parity report (legs L2/L3
queued — OM-20 conditional). No backfill, no `UPDATE`/`DELETE`, no re-mint of
existing claims, no `ingestion_permitted` flip, no HG gate tick, no merge/tag/
`main` push. No living-record pins. Schema change is one additive sqitch
change; `claim_content_digest_key` unchanged.
